# Project rules for Claude Code

This repo is graded on two things: the dApp, and how well we audit the code AI tools wrote for it. The process below exists so every claim in our AI Audit Report has evidence behind it. Follow it even when it feels slower.

## Before writing any code

- Read `docs/spec/spec-v1.md` first.
- If it still contains `TODO(decision)` markers, the spec is not frozen. Do not write contract code. Say which decisions are still open and stop.
- Every function you write must trace to a section of the spec. If the spec is silent or ambiguous on something you need, stop and ask. Do not invent requirements.

## Branches and tags

- Never commit to, rebase, or rewrite the `ai-baseline` branch, or move the `spec-v0` or `ai-baseline` tags.
- Never amend published commits or force-push.

## When a bug, vulnerability or spec gap is found

1. Run `scripts/new-issue.sh "<short title>"`. This creates `docs/issues/AUD-NNN-*.md`.
2. Write a regression test that FAILS on the current code. Commit it alone as `test(AUD-NNN): ...`.
3. Run `scripts/evidence.sh AUD-NNN-before`.
4. Fix the code. Commit as `fix(AUD-NNN): ...`.
5. Run `scripts/evidence.sh AUD-NNN-after`.
6. Fill in all four sections of the issue file. Do not set Status to fixed without both evidence runs.

In "Why the AI made the mistake", only state what the transcript or code shows. If you are guessing, start the line with `Hypothesis:`.

## Secrets

- Never read `.env` or print private keys, RPC keys or API keys. AI transcripts in this repo are committed to git.
- Only testnet burner wallets are used in this project.

## Commit message prefixes

| Prefix | Use for |
|---|---|
| `ai:` | Code generated by an AI tool and committed with little or no human change |
| `human:` | Code written or substantially rewritten by a person |
| `test(AUD-NNN):` | Regression test for an issue |
| `fix(AUD-NNN):` | Fix for an issue |
| `docs:` | Spec, report, issue files |
| `evidence:` | Evidence runs, testnet logs |
| `chore:` | Tooling and config |

## Rules learned from audit findings

Append a rule here each time an audit finding shows the AI making a mistake it could repeat. Every rule must cite the issue it came from. This section is part of our specification engineering evidence, so never delete old rules; mark them superseded instead.

- AUD-004: A whitelist mapping alone does not restrict ERC-20 movement. Enforce sender and recipient eligibility in OpenZeppelin's transfer hook and execute a direct-transfer regression; skipped tests are not passing behavioral evidence. Apply the latest explicit requirements when revocation semantics differ from the historical spec.
- AUD-005: Before testing an invariant, check it against every later requirements file. If a later requirement makes it false, restate it in the spec in the same change. Never name a test after an invariant unless the test would fail when that invariant is broken.
- AUD-006: A stored `issuer` or owner field is not proof of authority. Test every role path that touches it (grant, revoke, renounce, hand-over) and any state, such as escrowed tokens, that becomes unrecoverable when the role is gone.
- AUD-007: "No `receive`/`fallback`" does not mean "cannot receive ETH": `selfdestruct` and coinbase rewards force it in. For every contract that holds ETH, test forced ETH, and provide a way to recover any balance above what is owed.
- AUD-008: Implement each function against both the §5 function table and the §3 roles table. A role restriction stated only in §3 is still a revert condition.
- AUD-006, AUD-007: Write a regression's behaviour assertion first and await it (e.g. `await expect(tx).to.revert(ethers)`), then assert the error name. A test that fails only because an error or function is missing from the ABI does not show a behavioural failure, and an un-awaited transaction can leak into the next test.
- AUD-009: Preserve multi-transaction form input across public registry refreshes. Separately invalidate account-dependent data on wallet/chain changes; test approval and deposit as two consecutive user actions.
- AUD-010: A receipt timeout is not a failed transaction. Preserve its hash, keep duplicate submission blocked, and verify an actual receipt before reporting success or a revert.
- AUD-011: An `npm ci` that passes proves the lockfile works only on the machine that wrote it. After any dependency change, keep `test/FrontendLockfile.regression.test.ts` passing (every optional dependency has a lock entry). Do not claim a clean install for other platforms unless one was actually run there.
- AUD-012: A passing test suite does not show that the code has room to grow. Before tagging any change to a contract that `AssetFactory` deploys, record the runtime bytecode size of all three contracts against the EIP-170 limit (24 576 bytes) in the evidence. Deploy to public networks only with the optimised `production` profile.

# AUD-013: Transaction history shows a forced transfer as an ordinary transfer sent by the holder

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | fixed |
| Severity | low |
| Category | frontend |
| Found by (method) | manual review of the D5 branch against the Phase 4 frontend (`frontend/src/services/history.ts`) |
| Found by (person) | Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), session 069871d2, the same session that generated D5. Not an independent review |
| Location | `frontend/src/services/history.ts:42` (Transfer-only token query) and its event switch, at 71113cc (D5 branch, after `ai-baseline-d5`) |
| AI session that produced the code | History: [Phase 4 summary](../ai-logs/phase4-session.md) (Codex). `ForcedTransfer` event: D5, session 069871d2 |
| Baseline commit | 714366d (`ai-baseline-d5`); history code from f943f9c (`ai-baseline-phase4`) |
| Regression test commit | 5bdeded |
| Fix commit | 7da8dda |

## What is wrong

D5's `forcedTransfer` emits two events in one transaction: OpenZeppelin's `Transfer(from, to, amount)` and `ForcedTransfer(from, to, amount)`. The Phase 4 history service queried the token only for `Transfer`, plus `WhitelistUpdated` in admin views:

```ts
logs(token, token.filters.Transfer(), from, to),
```

As a result, every forced transfer appeared as type "Transfer" with `from` set to the holder. To the holder, the recipient and the admin, an issuer confiscation looked like a transfer the holder chose to make. Phase 4 §8.4 requires each history row to show its "Transaction type". It also requires that one operation emitting two events (there, a purchase) is not shown twice.

## 1. Why the AI made the mistake

What the code shows:
- The Phase 4 history code was correct for the contracts it was written against. When f943f9c was made, `AssetToken` had no forced-transfer path, and `docs/phase4-implementation.md` says "No pause/freeze … capability is invented".
- The D5 session added a new event to `AssetToken` and regenerated the frontend ABI. It then ran the frontend suite, which passed, and did not check which frontend code consumes token events. Every existing history test mocks only `Transfer`, so no test could notice a new event type.

Hypothesis: when a contract change only adds code, it looks safe for existing consumers because nothing they call has changed. But code that reads events or logs still changes its meaning when a new operation reuses an existing event, as `forcedTransfer` reuses `Transfer`.

## 2. Why it is a problem

The activity feed is the investor's record of what happened to their holding. After a lost-key or compliance recovery, the investor's own history would claim they sent the tokens. The issuer's view would also hide that an override power was used. This misstates both who acted and why, which undermines the transparency claim in spec-v1 §1 ("trusted issuer, transparent ledger"). No funds or on-chain state are affected.

## 3. How we fixed it

7da8dda:
- Reads all token events with one `"*"` query per block range, as the sale contract is already read. This keeps a single token request per range, which the existing outage test (`surfaces an RPC outage…`) requires.
- Maps `ForcedTransfer` to a "Forced transfer" row.
- Drops the paired `Transfer` row with the same hash, from, to and amount, the same way a purchase's `Transfer` is already dropped.
- Includes "Forced transfer" in the investor (account) view.

Also, 532abab adds a forced-transfer and pause step to the local integration lifecycle, so the fix is checked against real logs decoded by ethers and not only against mocks.

New CLAUDE.md rule: see the AUD-013 entry under "Rules learned from audit findings".

## 4. Evidence the fix works

- Regression test: `frontend/src/test/history.test.ts` :: `shows a forced transfer once, typed as forced, to the holder, the recipient and the admin view`.
- Before: `docs/evidence/aud-013/history-test-before.log` (1 failed / 4 passed: `expected { …(10) } to match object { type: 'Forced transfer', … }`). Contract suite at the test commit: `docs/evidence/runs/20261104T060403Z_5bdeded-dirty_AUD-013-before/` (129 passing; the regression is in the frontend suite, which `evidence.sh` does not run).
- After: `docs/evidence/aud-013/frontend-tests-after.log` (113 passed). `docs/evidence/aud-013/integration-after.log`: the real-node lifecycle passes, with one "Forced transfer" row, no duplicate "Transfer", and a paused token rejecting a transfer. Contract suite: AFTER_RUN.
- Observed while producing this evidence: the first integration run failed because `evidence.sh`'s coverage step leaves instrumented artifacts (factory 31 817 bytes, above EIP-170) that the integration test deploys directly. It passed after `npx hardhat compile --force`. This is a pre-existing tooling interaction, not part of this defect. It is logged as a follow-up in `docs/d5-implementation.md`.

# D5 implementation and review: pause and forced transfer

Date: 3–4 November 2026. Tool: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), session 069871d2, directed by Chordia Laksh. The transcript is archived by the hook under `docs/ai-logs/raw/`.

## What was decided

D5 was opened on 23 October 2026 and decided on 3 November 2026. Pause and forced transfer are implemented. Freeze is dropped, because whitelist revocation already blocks a holder from sending, receiving and buying. The normative rows are spec-v1 §5 "D5 functions", with invariants 1, 5, 6 and 7 restated. The reasons are in `docs/spec/phase3-requirements.md`, "D5 decision". Claude Code proposed each option, and the user adopted every recommendation.

## What was built (tag `ai-baseline-d5`, 714366d)

| Spec row / invariant | Implementation |
|---|---|
| `pause()` / `unpause()`, caller `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` | OpenZeppelin `Pausable`. `_update` calls `_requireNotPaused()`, so `transfer`, `transferFrom` and AssetSale's `allocate`, `buyTokens` and `recoverUnsoldTokens` revert with `EnforcedPause` |
| `forcedTransfer(from, to, amount)`, caller `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` | Reverts with `ForcedTransferFromZeroAddress` (a zero source would mint), `ForcedTransferFromWhitelisted(from)` or `RecipientNotWhitelisted(to)`. Calls ERC20's `_update` directly, which bypasses pause and the sender check. Emits `Transfer` and `ForcedTransfer` |
| Invariants 5, 6, 7 | `test/AssetToken.D5.test.ts` (21 tests after review), including a pairwise sweep of every source and recipient for invariant 6 |

Mutation check (`docs/evidence/d5/mutation.log`): removing the pause check, the zero-source check or the whitelisted-source check, or routing `forcedTransfer` through the overridden `_update`, makes the D5 suite fail. All 4 of 4 mutants were killed.

## Review before merge

This review was done by the same session that wrote the code, so it is **not independent**. Audit-1 had the same limitation. It covered the contract diff against spec-v1 §3 and §5, the CLAUDE.md rules, and every frontend consumer of the token's ABI and events.

| Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|
| AssetFactory runtime is exactly 24 576 bytes (EIP-170 limit) on the unoptimised profile used by `deploy:sepolia` | [AUD-012](issues/AUD-012-assetfactory-is-exactly-at-the-eip-170-size-limit-.md), fixed: the Sepolia deploy uses the `production` profile (13 545 bytes) |
| History shows a forced transfer as an ordinary `Transfer` sent by the holder | [AUD-013](issues/AUD-013-transaction-history-shows-a-forced-transfer-as-an-.md), fixed |
| D5 tests covered granting `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` but not revoking or renouncing it (CLAUDE.md AUD-006 rule) | Tests added in f1c1534. They pass, so there is no defect |
| Contract logic against the D5 table: caller, preconditions, events and every revert condition | No defect found |

Observations, not changed in this merge:
- **Delegating `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` now delegates confiscation.** A delegated admin can grant itself `COMPLIANCE_ROLE`, revoke a holder and force-transfer their balance to any whitelisted address. Before D5, the most it could do was block a holder. The frontend never grants this role (it only restores `COMPLIANCE_ROLE` to the connected wallet), but a direct contract call can. The trust model in spec-v1 §1 ("the issuer is trusted") now extends to anyone the issuer makes an admin.
- **Paused-token errors are generic.** The frontend shows "Contract rejected the request: EnforcedPause." because `frontend/src/utils/errors.ts` has no message for it. The UI has no pause or forced-transfer controls, and spec-v1 §7 does not require any.
- **The default profile has 0 bytes of headroom.** AUD-012 fixed the Sepolia path only. Any further growth in `AssetToken`, `AssetSale` or `AssetFactory` makes local deploys and the test suite fail until the optimizer is enabled for `default`.
- **`evidence.sh` leaves coverage-instrumented artifacts** (factory 31 817 bytes). `npm run test:integration` deploys straight from `artifacts/`, so after an evidence run it fails at factory deployment until `npx hardhat compile --force` is run. This predates D5.

## Results at merge

- Contracts: AFTER_COUNT. Evidence run: AFTER_RUN.
- Frontend: 113 tests passed (`docs/evidence/aud-013/frontend-tests-after.log`). The build succeeds.
- Local integration lifecycle against a real Hardhat node: passes, including the new forced-transfer and pause steps (`docs/evidence/aud-013/integration-after.log`).
- Not done: a real Sepolia deployment (AUD-003), and browser or MetaMask checks of the new behaviour.

So "freeze" in this spec now means revoking eligibility with `setWhitelisted(addr, false)`. The governing function rows are in §5 under "D5 functions", and invariants 1, 5, 6 and 7 are restated. Everywhere else, a mention of freeze (§1 "Why a blockchain", the §3 issuer row, the §4 `frozen` mapping and feature list, the §5 `freeze` / `unfreeze` rows) is superseded and kept only for audit comparison. # AUD-001: Core contracts and compliance controls are unimplemented

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | open |
| Severity | high |
| Category | logic |
| Found by (method) | manual code review and command execution |
| Found by (person) | Codex |
| Location | contracts/AssetToken.sol:8; contracts/AssetFactory.sol:9; contracts/AssetSale.sol:8, baseline c504215 |
| AI session that produced the code | Unknown; no attribution inferred |
| Baseline commit | c504215 |
| Regression test commit | None |
| Fix commit | None |

## What is wrong

Spec §§4–6 are largely unimplemented. Factory and sale expose only constructor state; authorisation, creation, allocation, buying and withdrawal are absent. AssetToken inherits unrestricted ERC-20 transfers and never enforces whitelist, pause or freeze. An issuer can transfer to any non-whitelisted wallet, violating the whitelist invariant.

## 1. Why the AI made the mistake

The source explicitly labels these areas as future phases. The original generation transcript was not inspected; no causal claim is made.

## 2. Why it is a problem

The application cannot satisfy its frozen specification or support an end-to-end demonstration. A successful compile or zero-exit test command does not establish working behavior.

## 3. How we fixed it

Open; no implementation change made during verification. Required next work: Implement the specified contract functions and compliance checks, then add executable access-control, transfer, sale and invariant tests.

## 4. Evidence the fix works

No fix or regression result is claimed. See `docs/VERIFICATION.md` for observed command results and limitations.

## Phase 2 follow-up — 23 October 2026

The token portion is now implemented under the later Phase 2 requirements, with the transfer bypass verified in AUD-004. This issue remains open because factory and sale functions belong to Phase 3 and remain placeholders. Pause/freeze/forced-transfer features from the historical spec are outside the current Phase 2 scope. See `docs/phase2-implementation.md`.

## Phase 3 follow-up — 23 October 2026

AssetFactory and AssetSale are now implemented under `docs/spec/phase3-requirements.md` (commit e407edf), covering authorisation, creation, registry, allocation, buying, withdrawal and close/recover. `npx hardhat test` reports 99 passing, 0 pending (`docs/evidence/phase3/test-full.log`). This issue remains open only for pause, freeze and forced transfer (spec-v1 §4–6, invariants 5–6), which await a team decision. See `docs/phase3-implementation.md`.

## D5 follow-up — 3 November 2026

D5 is decided: pause and forced transfer will be implemented, and freeze is dropped as already covered by whitelist revocation (`docs/spec/phase3-requirements.md`, "D5 decision"; spec-v1 §5 "D5 functions"). This issue remains open until `pause`, `unpause` and `forcedTransfer` are implemented and tested.

# AUD-013: Transaction history shows a forced transfer as an ordinary transfer sent by the holder

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | fixed |
| Severity | low |
| Category | frontend |
| Found by (method) | manual review of the D5 branch against the Phase 4 frontend (`frontend/src/services/history.ts`) |
| Found by (person) | Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), session 069871d2, the same session that generated D5. Not an independent review |
| Location | `frontend/src/services/history.ts:42` (Transfer-only token query) and its event switch, at 71113cc (D5 branch, after `ai-baseline-d5`) |
| AI session that produced the code | History: [Phase 4 summary](../ai-logs/phase4-session.md) (Codex). `ForcedTransfer` event: D5, session 069871d2 |
| Baseline commit | 714366d (`ai-baseline-d5`); history code from f943f9c (`ai-baseline-phase4`) |
| Regression test commit | 5bdeded |
| Fix commit | 7da8dda |

## What is wrong

D5's `forcedTransfer` emits two events in one transaction: OpenZeppelin's `Transfer(from, to, amount)` and `ForcedTransfer(from, to, amount)`. The Phase 4 history service queried the token only for `Transfer`, plus `WhitelistUpdated` in admin views:

```ts
logs(token, token.filters.Transfer(), from, to),
```

As a result, every forced transfer appeared as type "Transfer" with `from` set to the holder. To the holder, the recipient and the admin, an issuer confiscation looked like a transfer the holder chose to make. Phase 4 §8.4 requires each history row to show its "Transaction type". It also requires that one operation emitting two events (there, a purchase) is not shown twice.

## 1. Why the AI made the mistake

What the code shows:
- The Phase 4 history code was correct for the contracts it was written against. When f943f9c was made, `AssetToken` had no forced-transfer path, and `docs/phase4-implementation.md` says "No pause/freeze … capability is invented".
- The D5 session added a new event to `AssetToken` and regenerated the frontend ABI. It then ran the frontend suite, which passed, and did not check which frontend code consumes token events. Every existing history test mocks only `Transfer`, so no test could notice a new event type.

Hypothesis: when a contract change only adds code, it looks safe for existing consumers because nothing they call has changed. But code that reads events or logs still changes its meaning when a new operation reuses an existing event, as `forcedTransfer` reuses `Transfer`.

## 2. Why it is a problem

The activity feed is the investor's record of what happened to their holding. After a lost-key or compliance recovery, the investor's own history would claim they sent the tokens. The issuer's view would also hide that an override power was used. This misstates both who acted and why, which undermines the transparency claim in spec-v1 §1 ("trusted issuer, transparent ledger"). No funds or on-chain state are affected.

## 3. How we fixed it

7da8dda:
- Reads all token events with one `"*"` query per block range, as the sale contract is already read. This keeps a single token request per range, which the existing outage test (`surfaces an RPC outage…`) requires.
- Maps `ForcedTransfer` to a "Forced transfer" row.
- Drops the paired `Transfer` row with the same hash, from, to and amount, the same way a purchase's `Transfer` is already dropped.
- Includes "Forced transfer" in the investor (account) view.

Also, 532abab adds a forced-transfer and pause step to the local integration lifecycle, so the fix is checked against real logs decoded by ethers and not only against mocks.

New CLAUDE.md rule: see the AUD-013 entry under "Rules learned from audit findings".

## 4. Evidence the fix works

- Regression test: `frontend/src/test/history.test.ts` :: `shows a forced transfer once, typed as forced, to the holder, the recipient and the admin view`.
- Before: `docs/evidence/aud-013/history-test-before.log` (1 failed / 4 passed: `expected { …(10) } to match object { type: 'Forced transfer', … }`). Contract suite at the test commit: `docs/evidence/runs/20261104T060403Z_5bdeded-dirty_AUD-013-before/` (129 passing; the regression is in the frontend suite, which `evidence.sh` does not run).
- After: `docs/evidence/aud-013/frontend-tests-after.log` (113 passed). `docs/evidence/aud-013/integration-after.log`: the real-node lifecycle passes, with one "Forced transfer" row, no duplicate "Transfer", and a paused token rejecting a transfer. Contract suite: AFTER_RUN.
- Observed while producing this evidence: the first integration run failed because `evidence.sh`'s coverage step leaves instrumented artifacts (factory 31 817 bytes, above EIP-170) that the integration test deploys directly. It passed after `npx hardhat compile --force`. This is a pre-existing tooling interaction, not part of this defect. It is logged as a follow-up in `docs/d5-implementation.md`.

# D5 implementation and review: pause and forced transfer

Date: 3–4 November 2026. Tool: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), session 069871d2, directed by Chordia Laksh. The transcript is archived by the hook under `docs/ai-logs/raw/`.

## What was decided

D5 was opened on 23 October 2026 and decided on 3 November 2026. Pause and forced transfer are implemented. Freeze is dropped, because whitelist revocation already blocks a holder from sending, receiving and buying. The normative rows are spec-v1 §5 "D5 functions", with invariants 1, 5, 6 and 7 restated. The reasons are in `docs/spec/phase3-requirements.md`, "D5 decision". Claude Code proposed each option, and the user adopted every recommendation.

## What was built (tag `ai-baseline-d5`, 714366d)

| Spec row / invariant | Implementation |
|---|---|
| `pause()` / `unpause()`, caller `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` | OpenZeppelin `Pausable`. `_update` calls `_requireNotPaused()`, so `transfer`, `transferFrom` and AssetSale's `allocate`, `buyTokens` and `recoverUnsoldTokens` revert with `EnforcedPause` |
| `forcedTransfer(from, to, amount)`, caller `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` | Reverts with `ForcedTransferFromZeroAddress` (a zero source would mint), `ForcedTransferFromWhitelisted(from)` or `RecipientNotWhitelisted(to)`. Calls ERC20's `_update` directly, which bypasses pause and the sender check. Emits `Transfer` and `ForcedTransfer` |
| Invariants 5, 6, 7 | `test/AssetToken.D5.test.ts` (21 tests after review), including a pairwise sweep of every source and recipient for invariant 6 |

Mutation check (`docs/evidence/d5/mutation.log`): removing the pause check, the zero-source check or the whitelisted-source check, or routing `forcedTransfer` through the overridden `_update`, makes the D5 suite fail. All 4 of 4 mutants were killed.

## Review before merge

This review was done by the same session that wrote the code, so it is **not independent**. Audit-1 had the same limitation. It covered the contract diff against spec-v1 §3 and §5, the CLAUDE.md rules, and every frontend consumer of the token's ABI and events.

| Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|
| AssetFactory runtime is exactly 24 576 bytes (EIP-170 limit) on the unoptimised profile used by `deploy:sepolia` | [AUD-012](issues/AUD-012-assetfactory-is-exactly-at-the-eip-170-size-limit-.md), fixed: the Sepolia deploy uses the `production` profile (13 545 bytes) |
| History shows a forced transfer as an ordinary `Transfer` sent by the holder | [AUD-013](issues/AUD-013-transaction-history-shows-a-forced-transfer-as-an-.md), fixed |
| D5 tests covered granting `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` but not revoking or renouncing it (CLAUDE.md AUD-006 rule) | Tests added in f1c1534. They pass, so there is no defect |
| Contract logic against the D5 table: caller, preconditions, events and every revert condition | No defect found |

Observations, not changed in this merge:
- **Delegating `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` now delegates confiscation.** A delegated admin can grant itself `COMPLIANCE_ROLE`, revoke a holder and force-transfer their balance to any whitelisted address. Before D5, the most it could do was block a holder. The frontend never grants this role (it only restores `COMPLIANCE_ROLE` to the connected wallet), but a direct contract call can. The trust model in spec-v1 §1 ("the issuer is trusted") now extends to anyone the issuer makes an admin.
- **Paused-token errors are generic.** The frontend shows "Contract rejected the request: EnforcedPause." because `frontend/src/utils/errors.ts` has no message for it. The UI has no pause or forced-transfer controls, and spec-v1 §7 does not require any.
- **The default profile has 0 bytes of headroom.** AUD-012 fixed the Sepolia path only. Any further growth in `AssetToken`, `AssetSale` or `AssetFactory` makes local deploys and the test suite fail until the optimizer is enabled for `default`.
- **`evidence.sh` leaves coverage-instrumented artifacts** (factory 31 817 bytes). `npm run test:integration` deploys straight from `artifacts/`, so after an evidence run it fails at factory deployment until `npx hardhat compile --force` is run. This predates D5.

## Results at merge

- Contracts: AFTER_COUNT. Evidence run: AFTER_RUN.
- Frontend: 113 tests passed (`docs/evidence/aud-013/frontend-tests-after.log`). The build succeeds.
- Local integration lifecycle against a real Hardhat node: passes, including the new forced-transfer and pause steps (`docs/evidence/aud-013/integration-after.log`).
- Not done: a real Sepolia deployment (AUD-003), and browser or MetaMask checks of the new behaviour.

Useful commands when writing the report:

```bash
git log --oneline --grep '^ai:'            # what the AI wrote
git log --oneline --grep '^fix(AUD'        # every fix
git diff --stat ai-baseline..main          # how far we moved from the AI output
git log --format='%an' | sort | uniq -c    # commits per person
```

Phase 4 additions (28 October 2026, uncommitted by user instruction):

- Specification and prompt: `docs/spec/phase4-requirements.md`.
- Current architecture/workflows/status: `docs/phase4-implementation.md`.
- Curated AI decisions and actual errors: `docs/ai-logs/phase4-session.md`.

content.text:
D5 is reviewed and merged into `main` as `654d68c`. The review found one more bug (AUD-013) and a gap in my own tests, both fixed before the merge. This was a self-review: I wrote D5 in this same session, so it isn't independent, and `docs/d5-implementation.md` and the AI-log row say so.

**What the review found:**

| Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Contract logic against the spec: callers, preconditions, events and every revert condition | No defect found |
| **AUD-013:** after D5, a forced transfer showed up in the activity history as an ordinary transfer sent by the holder. Phase 4 §8.4 requires the transaction type to be correct | Fixed with the full workflow (`5bdeded` failing test → `7da8dda` fix). The history now reads all token events in one query and shows each forced transfer once, as "Forced transfer" |
| My D5 tests checked granting `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` to a delegate, but not revoking or renouncing it. CLAUDE.md's AUD-006 rule requires both | Tests added (`f1c1534`). They pass, so there was no defect |

I also added a forced-transfer and pause step to the local integration test. It runs against a real Hardhat node, so the AUD-013 fix is checked against real event logs and not only mocks.

**Verified at the merged commit:**
- 131 contract tests pass, line coverage 98.79%.
- 113 frontend tests pass, and the frontend build succeeds.
- The integration test passes against the real node.

**Doc updates that went with the merge:**
- AUD-001 is closed.
- spec-v1 now says D5 is implemented. It also notes that granting `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` now means trusting that person with confiscation.
- Phase 4's "remain unsupported" paragraph has a note saying it's outdated.
- `docs/d5-implementation.md` has the review summary.
- `docs/ai-logs/INDEX.md` has a row for this session. I also fixed a blank line from the Phase 4 merge that was splitting that table.
- REPORT-MAP §4 now lists the per-phase baseline tags.
- CLAUDE.md has a new rule for AUD-013.

**Left open (also recorded in `docs/d5-implementation.md`):**
- **Size limit on local builds:** without the optimizer, `AssetFactory` is still exactly 24,576 bytes. The next contract change will break local deploys and the tests unless the optimizer is turned on for the default profile.
- **Evidence-run trap:** `evidence.sh`'s coverage step leaves oversized coverage builds in `artifacts/`. If you run `npm run test:integration` afterwards, it fails at deployment until you run `npx hardhat compile --force`. This predates D5, and it caught me during this check.
- **Paused-token message:** the frontend shows the generic "Contract rejected the request: EnforcedPause." There are no pause or forced-transfer buttons in the UI, which spec §7 doesn't require.

**Still to do:**
- Redact the teammate's email at `exports/2026-10-23-phase3-and-audit-remediation.txt:2635`, then commit the transcripts.
- Confirm adityamd-1307 agrees with D5.
- `README.md` is still out of date.
- Do the Sepolia deployment (AUD-003).
- Push. Nothing is pushed yet: `main` is several commits ahead of `origin`, plus the D5 branch and the `ai-baseline-phase4` / `ai-baseline-d5` tags. Tell me when you want that done.

# SC4053 Blockchain Technology — Phase 3: Asset Registry and Primary Issuance

The text below is the user's Phase 3 request, given to Claude Code on 23 October 2026. Table formatting was lost when it was pasted and has been restored as Markdown; the wording is unchanged. The decisions in the final section were made by the user in the same session, in answer to questions raised by Claude Code about conflicts with `spec-v1.md`.

---

Deliverable: Functional on-chain asset issuance and purchase

Objective: Let authorised issuers create multiple tokenised assets and sell them to eligible investors.

This is where your project develops beyond a simple ERC-20 token demonstration.

## Task 3.1 — Implement AssetFactory.sol

The factory will act as the entry point for new asset issuance.

It should provide these functions:

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `authorizeIssuer(address)` | Platform admin grants issuer permission |
| `revokeIssuer(address)` | Platform admin removes issuer creation permission |
| `createAsset(...)` | Authorised issuer creates an asset |
| `getAsset(assetId)` | Returns asset metadata and contract addresses |
| `getAssetCount()` | Returns number of registered assets |

A successful `createAsset()` should deploy an AssetToken and associated AssetSale, then record the asset in the registry.

Suggested metadata:

```text
assetId
name
symbol
description
assetType
totalSupply
tokenContract
saleContract
issuerAddress
unitPriceWei
```

The asset ID should be generated automatically rather than supplied by the issuer.

## Task 3.2 — Implement AssetSale.sol

This contract will facilitate primary-market purchases.

Essential variables:

```solidity
IERC20 public assetToken;
address public issuer;
uint256 public pricePerToken;
```

Main function:

```solidity
buyTokens(uint256 quantity) external payable
```

Purchase validation must confirm:

- The buyer is an approved investor.
- Quantity is greater than zero.
- Enough tokens remain in the sale contract.
- `msg.value` equals `quantity * pricePerToken`.

If every condition passes, the contract transfers tokens to the investor and records the purchase event.

Use exact payment for the MVP; partial payments, complex refunds and variable pricing are unnecessary.

## Task 3.3 — Implement the inventory funding process

The issuer must allocate tokens to the sale contract before buyers can purchase them.

The lifecycle will be:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Issuer creates an asset | 10,000 CPT minted to issuer |
| Issuer whitelists the sale contract | Contract is permitted to hold and transfer CPT |
| Issuer deposits 5,000 CPT for sale | Sale contract now has purchasable inventory |
| Investor buys 100 CPT | Investor pays 0.1 testnet ETH and receives 100 CPT |

To simplify the MVP, the price is fixed at asset creation. Later changes to the sale price are not supported.

## Task 3.4 — Implement issuer withdrawals

Create an issuer-only withdrawal function for sale proceeds.

The function must prevent unauthorised withdrawals and account for reentrancy risks when sending ETH. Include a protected way to recover any unsold token inventory if the sale is closed.

## Task 3.5 — Test factory and sale contracts

Test the following scenarios:

| Test case | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Unauthorised wallet creates an asset | Revert |
| Authorised issuer creates asset | Token and sale contracts deployed |
| Issuer creates two different assets | Both registered independently |
| Whitelisted investor buys 100 tokens | Correct ETH payment and token transfer |
| Investor underpays | Revert |
| Investor overpays | Revert |
| Investor buys more than inventory | Revert |
| Unapproved investor attempts purchase | Revert |
| Non-issuer withdraws proceeds | Revert |

Phase 3 completion criteria: From a Hardhat script or console, you should be able to register an issuer, create an asset, whitelist an investor, fund the sale contract, execute a purchase and inspect the updated balances.

You now have a working blockchain backend.

---

## Additional constraints from the session brief

- Implement AssetFactory and AssetSale only. Do not add pause, freeze or forced transfer to AssetToken in this phase; that needs a separate team decision.
- `withdrawProceeds` must follow checks-effects-interactions (spec-v1 §4 reentrancy requirement, invariant 8).
- `revokeIssuer` only blocks future `createAsset` calls. Contracts the issuer has already deployed keep operating (spec-v1 §5 note on `deauthoriseIssuer`).

## Decisions made by the user (23 October 2026)

Claude Code raised these conflicts between this request and `spec-v1.md` before writing code. The user chose:

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | spec-v1 and this request name functions and variables differently. Which governs? | **This request governs**, as Phase 2's requirements did. Use `authorizeIssuer`, `revokeIssuer`, `getAsset`, `getAssetCount`, `buyTokens`, `pricePerToken` and `assetToken`. spec-v1 names (`authoriseIssuer`, `deauthoriseIssuer`, `buy`, `priceWei`, `token`) are superseded. The test stub titles are updated to match. |
| D2 | What does `createAsset` take as metadata? | `createAsset(name, symbol, description, assetType, totalSupply, unitPriceWei)`. `assetType` is an enum: `AssetType { RealWorld, Digital }`. `assetId` is assigned automatically. |
| D3 | How is unsold inventory recovered? | An issuer-only, irreversible `closeSale()`. After closing, `buyTokens` and `allocate` revert, and an issuer-only `recoverUnsoldTokens()` returns the sale contract's entire token balance to the issuer. |
| D4 | The repo was mid-rebase of `fix/spec-corrections-phase1`. | Abort the rebase and merge the branch into `main` normally, so no published history is rewritten. |
| D5 | Pause, freeze and forced transfer (spec-v1 §4–6, invariants 5–6) have been deferred twice, with no final decision (audit-1 F-06). | **Still open.** The user decided to keep these deferred, but with an owner and a deadline. Owners: Chordia Laksh and adityamd-1307, jointly. Due before Phase 4 starts. No code is written for these features until D5 is decided. The research session rated them "Must" (research R296–297), so if they are dropped, the report must justify it. **Decided 3 November 2026** (see below). |
| D6 | The issuer could renounce, or have revoked, the roles that `token.issuer()` claims they hold. That can lock sale inventory permanently (audit-1 F-05). | The `issuer`'s `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` on AssetToken can never be renounced or revoked. `COMPLIANCE_ROLE` stays delegable and revocable: the issuer can always grant it back, and the Phase 2 admin/compliance separation (test at `AssetToken.test.ts:209`) is kept. Invariant 7 is restated: the `issuer` always holds `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` on their own token. The user first chose to lock both roles, then narrowed this to the admin role once the conflict with that Phase 2 test was raised. |
| D7 | ETH forced into an AssetSale by `selfdestruct` or a coinbase reward is unrecoverable (audit-1 F-08). | Add an issuer-only `sweepExcessETH()` that sends `address(this).balance − unclaimedProceeds` to the issuer. Invariant 3 is restated: `unclaimedProceeds` equals total paid minus total withdrawn and is ≤ the ETH balance, and any excess can be swept. |
| D8 | The platform admin can authorise itself as an issuer, contrary to spec-v1 §3 (audit-1 F-10). | `authorizeIssuer(admin)` reverts. This is a policy check, not a security guarantee: the admin can still use a second wallet, and the factory cannot stop an issuer from whitelisting the admin as a buyer. |
| D9 | The raw transcripts contain team members' email addresses. | Commit them with every email address redacted except GitHub noreply addresses. The rule is applied by the archive hook and documented in `docs/ai-logs/README.md`. |

## D5 decision (3 November 2026)

Chordia Laksh decided this in a Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) session, as joint owner of D5 with adityamd-1307. It came after the deadline ("before Phase 4 starts"), because the phase-4 frontend work went ahead first. Claude Code proposed the main option and the three sub-choices, marking each as its recommendation. The user picked every recommendation. The normative rows are in spec-v1 §5 under "D5 functions", and invariants 1, 5, 6 and 7 are restated there.

| Question | Decision | Reason given in the session |
|---|---|---|
| Implement, drop, or split? | Implement `pause` / `unpause` and `forcedTransfer`. Drop `freeze` / `unfreeze`. | Since Phase 2 §2.3, revoking eligibility already blocks a holder from sending, receiving and buying while preserving the balance, which is all that freeze does. Without forced transfer, tokens at a revoked or lost-key address are stranded for good. Pause is cheap with OpenZeppelin. |
| Who may call them? | `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` | The issuer can never lose this role (D6). Authority comes from the role, not the stored `issuer` field (AUD-006 lesson). Keeps the strongest powers away from the delegable `COMPLIANCE_ROLE`. |
| Which holders can `forcedTransfer` take from? | Only non-whitelisted (revoked) addresses, never `address(0)` | Recovery becomes "revoke, then force-transfer", which mirrors spec-v1's "freeze, then forcedTransfer" flow. Live investors and the sale contract cannot be drained without an earlier on-chain revocation event. The zero-address check stops `forcedTransfer` from minting. |
| Does `forcedTransfer` work while paused? | Yes | As in spec-v1 §5 and invariant 5. Recovery stays possible during an emergency halt. |

# AI logs

Evidence for Report Sections 2, 3 and 8: which AI tools we used, what we gave them, and what came back.

## What is captured automatically

Claude Code sessions started inside this repo are copied into `raw/` by the hook in `.claude/hooks/archive_transcript.mjs`. It runs after every turn and when the session ends. `sessions.tsv` lists each session with the git user who ran it.

History of the hook:
- Until 23 October 2026 the hook ran `python3`. On Windows that is a Microsoft Store stub that does nothing, so no transcript was ever archived (audit-1 finding F-01).
- It now runs on `node`, which the project already requires.
- The three sessions that existed by then (Phase 1 setup, Phase 3, audit 1) were archived by running the hook by hand. Their `first_seen_utc` in `sessions.tsv` is therefore the archive time, not the session start.
- The Phase 2 Codex session ran outside Claude Code. No verbatim log of it is held; see `phase2-session.md`.

**Redaction.** The copies in `raw/` are verbatim except for one mechanical rule, applied by the hook: every email address is replaced with `[email-redacted]`. GitHub `@users.noreply.github.com` addresses are left alone, because they are already public in the commit history. This keeps team members' personal and work addresses out of a public repository. It is the only exception to "do not edit transcripts" below.

Claude Code only keeps its own transcripts for a limited time, so the copies in `raw/` are the record we rely on. Commit them.

The raw files are JSONL in Claude Code's internal format, which can change between versions. They are the record, not something to read. For the report, use the readable exports below.

## What you do by hand

1. **Name sessions** so they are easy to find: start Claude Code with `claude -n <topic>`, e.g. `claude -n token-contract-gen`.
2. **Export important sessions** before ending them: run `/export docs/ai-logs/exports/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<topic>.txt`. Do this for any session that generated code, changed the spec, or found a bug.
3. **Log other AI tools** (claude.ai chats, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor): save or copy the conversation into `exports/` and add a row to `INDEX.md`.
4. **Add an INDEX row** for every session that mattered. Skip trivial ones.

## Rules

- Never paste private keys, RPC URLs with keys, or API keys into any AI tool. These files are committed.
- Do not edit transcripts after the fact. If a session went badly, that is evidence too.

The teammate's email is redacted, adityamd-1307's agreement with D5 is on record, and the transcripts are committed. Nothing is pushed.

**`66dda95` (`docs:`)**
- **D5 agreement:** `phase3-requirements.md` records it, stating that you passed it on to me on 4 November after the merge and that it wasn't given in a logged session. That keeps the report from implying more than happened.

**`b769e4c` (`evidence:`)**
- I used the hook's own pattern and replacement text (`[email-redacted]`, keeping GitHub `noreply` addresses), so the export is redacted exactly like the raw files. Line 2635 now reads `[email-redacted], and an npm author email…`. The audit-1 export had no addresses.

- I scanned every one of those files before committing:

  - **Secrets:** no Hardhat dev keys, `Private Key:` lines from `hardhat node`, seed phrases or RPC/API keys. One match turned out to be a quoted search pattern that was already committed, not a secret.

The working tree is clean. The archive hook rewrites this session's raw transcript every time I finish a reply, so it will show as modified again after this one. Before pushing, it needs one more re-archive commit, with the same email and secret scan.

- **Push:** `main`, the D5 branch and the `ai-baseline-phase4` / `ai-baseline-d5` tags.

# SC4053 Blockchain Technology — Phase 3: Asset Registry and Primary Issuance

The text below is the user's Phase 3 request, given to Claude Code on 23 October 2026. Table formatting was lost when it was pasted and has been restored as Markdown; the wording is unchanged. The decisions in the final section were made by the user in the same session, in answer to questions raised by Claude Code about conflicts with `spec-v1.md`.

---

Deliverable: Functional on-chain asset issuance and purchase

Objective: Let authorised issuers create multiple tokenised assets and sell them to eligible investors.

This is where your project develops beyond a simple ERC-20 token demonstration.

## Task 3.1 — Implement AssetFactory.sol

The factory will act as the entry point for new asset issuance.

It should provide these functions:

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `authorizeIssuer(address)` | Platform admin grants issuer permission |
| `revokeIssuer(address)` | Platform admin removes issuer creation permission |
| `createAsset(...)` | Authorised issuer creates an asset |
| `getAsset(assetId)` | Returns asset metadata and contract addresses |
| `getAssetCount()` | Returns number of registered assets |

A successful `createAsset()` should deploy an AssetToken and associated AssetSale, then record the asset in the registry.

Suggested metadata:

```text
assetId
name
symbol
description
assetType
totalSupply
tokenContract
saleContract
issuerAddress
unitPriceWei
```

The asset ID should be generated automatically rather than supplied by the issuer.

## Task 3.2 — Implement AssetSale.sol

This contract will facilitate primary-market purchases.

Essential variables:

```solidity
IERC20 public assetToken;
address public issuer;
uint256 public pricePerToken;
```

Main function:

```solidity
buyTokens(uint256 quantity) external payable
```

Purchase validation must confirm:

- The buyer is an approved investor.
- Quantity is greater than zero.
- Enough tokens remain in the sale contract.
- `msg.value` equals `quantity * pricePerToken`.

If every condition passes, the contract transfers tokens to the investor and records the purchase event.

Use exact payment for the MVP; partial payments, complex refunds and variable pricing are unnecessary.

## Task 3.3 — Implement the inventory funding process

The issuer must allocate tokens to the sale contract before buyers can purchase them.

The lifecycle will be:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Issuer creates an asset | 10,000 CPT minted to issuer |
| Issuer whitelists the sale contract | Contract is permitted to hold and transfer CPT |
| Issuer deposits 5,000 CPT for sale | Sale contract now has purchasable inventory |
| Investor buys 100 CPT | Investor pays 0.1 testnet ETH and receives 100 CPT |

To simplify the MVP, the price is fixed at asset creation. Later changes to the sale price are not supported.

## Task 3.4 — Implement issuer withdrawals

Create an issuer-only withdrawal function for sale proceeds.

The function must prevent unauthorised withdrawals and account for reentrancy risks when sending ETH. Include a protected way to recover any unsold token inventory if the sale is closed.

## Task 3.5 — Test factory and sale contracts

Test the following scenarios:

| Test case | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Unauthorised wallet creates an asset | Revert |
| Authorised issuer creates asset | Token and sale contracts deployed |
| Issuer creates two different assets | Both registered independently |
| Whitelisted investor buys 100 tokens | Correct ETH payment and token transfer |
| Investor underpays | Revert |
| Investor overpays | Revert |
| Investor buys more than inventory | Revert |
| Unapproved investor attempts purchase | Revert |
| Non-issuer withdraws proceeds | Revert |

Phase 3 completion criteria: From a Hardhat script or console, you should be able to register an issuer, create an asset, whitelist an investor, fund the sale contract, execute a purchase and inspect the updated balances.

You now have a working blockchain backend.

---

## Additional constraints from the session brief

- Implement AssetFactory and AssetSale only. Do not add pause, freeze or forced transfer to AssetToken in this phase; that needs a separate team decision.
- `withdrawProceeds` must follow checks-effects-interactions (spec-v1 §4 reentrancy requirement, invariant 8).
- `revokeIssuer` only blocks future `createAsset` calls. Contracts the issuer has already deployed keep operating (spec-v1 §5 note on `deauthoriseIssuer`).

## Decisions made by the user (23 October 2026)

Claude Code raised these conflicts between this request and `spec-v1.md` before writing code. The user chose:

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | spec-v1 and this request name functions and variables differently. Which governs? | **This request governs**, as Phase 2's requirements did. Use `authorizeIssuer`, `revokeIssuer`, `getAsset`, `getAssetCount`, `buyTokens`, `pricePerToken` and `assetToken`. spec-v1 names (`authoriseIssuer`, `deauthoriseIssuer`, `buy`, `priceWei`, `token`) are superseded. The test stub titles are updated to match. |
| D2 | What does `createAsset` take as metadata? | `createAsset(name, symbol, description, assetType, totalSupply, unitPriceWei)`. `assetType` is an enum: `AssetType { RealWorld, Digital }`. `assetId` is assigned automatically. |
| D3 | How is unsold inventory recovered? | An issuer-only, irreversible `closeSale()`. After closing, `buyTokens` and `allocate` revert, and an issuer-only `recoverUnsoldTokens()` returns the sale contract's entire token balance to the issuer. |
| D4 | The repo was mid-rebase of `fix/spec-corrections-phase1`. | Abort the rebase and merge the branch into `main` normally, so no published history is rewritten. |
| D5 | Pause, freeze and forced transfer (spec-v1 §4–6, invariants 5–6) have been deferred twice, with no final decision (audit-1 F-06). | **Still open.** The user decided to keep these deferred, but with an owner and a deadline. Owners: Chordia Laksh and adityamd-1307, jointly. Due before Phase 4 starts. No code is written for these features until D5 is decided. The research session rated them "Must" (research R296–297), so if they are dropped, the report must justify it. **Decided 3 November 2026** (see below). |
| D6 | The issuer could renounce, or have revoked, the roles that `token.issuer()` claims they hold. That can lock sale inventory permanently (audit-1 F-05). | The `issuer`'s `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` on AssetToken can never be renounced or revoked. `COMPLIANCE_ROLE` stays delegable and revocable: the issuer can always grant it back, and the Phase 2 admin/compliance separation (test at `AssetToken.test.ts:209`) is kept. Invariant 7 is restated: the `issuer` always holds `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` on their own token. The user first chose to lock both roles, then narrowed this to the admin role once the conflict with that Phase 2 test was raised. |
| D7 | ETH forced into an AssetSale by `selfdestruct` or a coinbase reward is unrecoverable (audit-1 F-08). | Add an issuer-only `sweepExcessETH()` that sends `address(this).balance − unclaimedProceeds` to the issuer. Invariant 3 is restated: `unclaimedProceeds` equals total paid minus total withdrawn and is ≤ the ETH balance, and any excess can be swept. |
| D8 | The platform admin can authorise itself as an issuer, contrary to spec-v1 §3 (audit-1 F-10). | `authorizeIssuer(admin)` reverts. This is a policy check, not a security guarantee: the admin can still use a second wallet, and the factory cannot stop an issuer from whitelisting the admin as a buyer. |
| D9 | The raw transcripts contain team members' email addresses. | Commit them with every email address redacted except GitHub noreply addresses. The rule is applied by the archive hook and documented in `docs/ai-logs/README.md`. |

## D5 decision (3 November 2026)

Chordia Laksh decided this in a Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) session, as joint owner of D5 with adityamd-1307. adityamd-1307's agreement was relayed to that session by Chordia Laksh on 4 November 2026, after the code was merged. It was not given in a logged session. It came after the deadline ("before Phase 4 starts"), because the phase-4 frontend work went ahead first. Claude Code proposed the main option and the three sub-choices, marking each as its recommendation. The user picked every recommendation. The normative rows are in spec-v1 §5 under "D5 functions", and invariants 1, 5, 6 and 7 are restated there.

| Question | Decision | Reason given in the session |
|---|---|---|
| Implement, drop, or split? | Implement `pause` / `unpause` and `forcedTransfer`. Drop `freeze` / `unfreeze`. | Since Phase 2 §2.3, revoking eligibility already blocks a holder from sending, receiving and buying while preserving the balance, which is all that freeze does. Without forced transfer, tokens at a revoked or lost-key address are stranded for good. Pause is cheap with OpenZeppelin. |
| Who may call them? | `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` | The issuer can never lose this role (D6). Authority comes from the role, not the stored `issuer` field (AUD-006 lesson). Keeps the strongest powers away from the delegable `COMPLIANCE_ROLE`. |
| Which holders can `forcedTransfer` take from? | Only non-whitelisted (revoked) addresses, never `address(0)` | Recovery becomes "revoke, then force-transfer", which mirrors spec-v1's "freeze, then forcedTransfer" flow. Live investors and the sale contract cannot be drained without an earlier on-chain revocation event. The zero-address check stops `forcedTransfer` from minting. |
| Does `forcedTransfer` work while paused? | Yes | As in spec-v1 §5 and invariant 5. Recovery stays possible during an emergency halt. |

# AI logs

Evidence for Report Sections 2, 3 and 8: which AI tools we used, what we gave them, and what came back.

## What is captured automatically

Claude Code sessions started inside this repo are copied into `raw/` by the hook in `.claude/hooks/archive_transcript.mjs`. It runs after every turn and when the session ends. `sessions.tsv` lists each session with the git user who ran it.

History of the hook:
- Until 23 October 2026 the hook ran `python3`. On Windows that is a Microsoft Store stub that does nothing, so no transcript was ever archived (audit-1 finding F-01).
- It now runs on `node`, which the project already requires.
- The three sessions that existed by then (Phase 1 setup, Phase 3, audit 1) were archived by running the hook by hand. Their `first_seen_utc` in `sessions.tsv` is therefore the archive time, not the session start.
- The Phase 2 Codex session ran outside Claude Code. No verbatim log of it is held; see `phase2-session.md`.

**Redaction.** The copies in `raw/` are verbatim except for one mechanical rule, applied by the hook: every email address is replaced with `[email-redacted]`. GitHub `@users.noreply.github.com` addresses are left alone, because they are already public in the commit history. This keeps team members' personal and work addresses out of a public repository. It is the only exception to "do not edit transcripts" below. The same rule, with the hook's regular expression, is applied by hand to the readable copies in `exports/` before they are committed. On 4 November 2026 it replaced one address in `exports/2026-10-23-phase3-and-audit-remediation.txt` (line 2635).

Claude Code only keeps its own transcripts for a limited time, so the copies in `raw/` are the record we rely on. Commit them.

The raw files are JSONL in Claude Code's internal format, which can change between versions. They are the record, not something to read. For the report, use the readable exports below.

## What you do by hand

1. **Name sessions** so they are easy to find: start Claude Code with `claude -n <topic>`, e.g. `claude -n token-contract-gen`.
2. **Export important sessions** before ending them: run `/export docs/ai-logs/exports/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<topic>.txt`. Do this for any session that generated code, changed the spec, or found a bug.
3. **Log other AI tools** (claude.ai chats, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor): save or copy the conversation into `exports/` and add a row to `INDEX.md`.
4. **Add an INDEX row** for every session that mattered. Skip trivial ones.

## Rules

- Never paste private keys, RPC URLs with keys, or API keys into any AI tool. These files are committed.
- Do not edit transcripts after the fact. If a session went badly, that is evidence too.

# AUD-014: Default build profile leaves AssetFactory at the EIP-170 limit so local deploys and tests break on any contract growth

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | open |
| Severity | low |
| Category | other (build configuration / contract size) |
| Found by (method) | follow-up to AUD-012: the limitation recorded there as "Not changed" |
| Found by (person) | Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), session 069871d2. Fix requested by Chordia Laksh |
| Location | `hardhat.config.ts` `default` profile, at b89f4b6 |
| AI session that produced the code | Profiles: Phase 1 setup session (commit 9884a9b) |
| Baseline commit | b89f4b6 |
| Regression test commit | c97e068 |
| Fix commit | FIX_COMMIT |

## What is wrong

AUD-012 moved only `deploy:sepolia` to the optimised `production` profile. Every other Hardhat build still uses `default`, which has no optimizer settings: `npm test`, `npm run compile`, `deploy:local`, `deploy:ephemeral`, `demo:local` and `frontend:sync`. `npm run test:integration` also deploys straight from those `artifacts/`. On that profile, AssetFactory's runtime bytecode is exactly 24 576 bytes, the EIP-170 limit (`docs/evidence/d5/bytecode-sizes.txt`; `docs/evidence/aud-012/deploy-before.log`).

## 1. Why the AI made the mistake

What the code and transcript show:
- The Phase 1 session created an unoptimised `default` profile and an optimised `production` profile, but no script used `production` (AUD-012).
- During AUD-012, the user asked only for the Sepolia deploy to be switched. The issue file recorded the local paths as "Not changed", so this is a known, recorded limitation, not a missed one.
- The AUD-012 regression test checks `deploy:sepolia` only. It could not detect the same risk on the other build paths.

Hypothesis: the Phase 1 setup copied Hardhat 3's sample configuration, where `default` is unoptimised for fast compiles and readable traces, and `production` is meant for deployment. That split suits contracts with plenty of headroom, not a factory that embeds two other contracts.

## 2. Why it is a problem

With 0 bytes of headroom, any further growth in `AssetToken`, `AssetSale` or `AssetFactory` makes the factory larger than 24 576 bytes. `ethers.deployContract("AssetFactory", …)` then reverts in every test fixture, local deploy, demo seed and integration run. That blocks all further development until someone traces the failure back to contract size. There is no security impact.

## 3. How we fixed it

FIX_COMMIT enables the optimizer (200 runs, the same as `production`) in the `default` profile. `production` is kept, and `deploy:sepolia` still names it explicitly (AUD-012).

Consequence for evidence: gas figures in runs from FIX_COMMIT onward come from optimised bytecode. They are not comparable with earlier runs (`docs/evidence/runs/*/gas.log`).

New CLAUDE.md rule: see the AUD-014 entry under "Rules learned from audit findings".

## 4. Evidence the fix works

- Regression test: `test/DeployProfile.regression.test.ts` :: `every npm script that compiles through hardhat run, test or compile uses an optimised profile`. It reads every script in `package.json` and checks Hardhat's resolved config for each one's profile.
- Before: BEFORE_RUN (test fails: `npm run test: "default" solc 0.8.24 optimizer: expected undefined to equal true`).
- After: AFTER_RUN (test passes); SIZES; frontend and integration results in `docs/evidence/aud-014/`.

16	## What is wrong
17	
18	AUD-012 moved only `deploy:sepolia` to the optimised `production` profile. Every other Hardhat build still uses `default`, which has no optimizer settings: `npm test`, `npm run compile`, `deploy:local`, `deploy:ephemeral`, `demo:local` and `frontend:sync`. `npm run test:integration` also deploys straight from those `artifacts/`. On that profile, AssetFactory's runtime bytecode is exactly 24 576 bytes, the EIP-170 limit (`docs/evidence/d5/bytecode-sizes.txt`; `docs/evidence/aud-012/deploy-before.log`).
19	
20	## 1. Why the AI made the mistake
21	
22	What the code and transcript show:
...
27	Hypothesis: the Phase 1 setup copied Hardhat 3's sample configuration, where `default` is unoptimised for fast compiles and readable traces, and `production` is meant for deployment. That split suits contracts with plenty of headroom, not a factory that embeds two other contracts.
28	
29	## 2. Why it is a problem
30	
31	With 0 bytes of headroom, any further growth in `AssetToken`, `AssetSale` or `AssetFactory` makes the factory larger than 24 576 bytes. `ethers.deployContract("AssetFactory", …)` then reverts in every test fixture, local deploy, demo seed and integration run. That blocks all further development until someone traces the failure back to contract size. There is no security impact.
32	
33	## 3. How we fixed it
34	
35	e1fc698 enables the optimizer (200 runs, the same as `production`) in the `default` profile. `production` is kept, and `deploy:sepolia` still names it explicitly (AUD-012).
36	
37	Consequence for evidence: gas figures in runs from e1fc698 onward come from optimised bytecode. They are not comparable with earlier runs (`docs/evidence/runs/*/gas.log`).
38	
39	New CLAUDE.md rule: see the AUD-014 entry under "Rules learned from audit findings".
40	
41	## 4. Evidence the fix works
42	
43	- Regression test: `test/DeployProfile.regression.test.ts` :: `every npm script that compiles through hardhat run, test or compile uses an optimised profile`. It reads every script in `package.json` and checks Hardhat's resolved config for each one's profile.
44	- Before: `docs/evidence/runs/20261104T133014Z_c97e068-dirty_AUD-014-before/test.log` (131 passing, 1 failing: `npm run test: "default" solc 0.8.24 optimizer: expected undefined to equal true`).
45	- After: `docs/evidence/runs/20261104T133135Z_e1fc698-dirty_AUD-014-after/test.log` (132 passing; coverage unchanged at 98.79% lines, so the coverage step works with the optimizer on).
46	- Sizes: `docs/evidence/aud-014/bytecode-sizes.txt`. AssetFactory is 13 545 bytes (55.1%), down from 24 576.
47	- Frontend: `docs/evidence/aud-014/frontend-tests-after.log` (113 passed). Real-node integration: `docs/evidence/aud-014/integration-after.log` (passes).
48	- Side effect: the coverage-instrumented factory that `evidence.sh` leaves in `artifacts/` is now 19 944 bytes, below the limit; it was 31 817. `docs/evidence/aud-014/integration-after-evidence-run.log` shows `npm run test:integration` passing straight after an evidence run, with no recompile. That removes the trap recorded in `docs/d5-implementation.md` and AUD-013 §4.

# Project rules for Claude Code

This repo is graded on two things: the dApp, and how well we audit the code AI tools wrote for it. The process below exists so every claim in our AI Audit Report has evidence behind it. Follow it even when it feels slower.

## Before writing any code

- Read `docs/spec/spec-v1.md` first.
- If it still contains `TODO(decision)` markers, the spec is not frozen. Do not write contract code. Say which decisions are still open and stop.
- Every function you write must trace to a section of the spec. If the spec is silent or ambiguous on something you need, stop and ask. Do not invent requirements.

## Branches and tags

- Never commit to, rebase, or rewrite the `ai-baseline` branch, or move the `spec-v0` or `ai-baseline` tags.
- Never amend published commits or force-push.

## When a bug, vulnerability or spec gap is found

1. Run `scripts/new-issue.sh "<short title>"`. This creates `docs/issues/AUD-NNN-*.md`.
2. Write a regression test that FAILS on the current code. Commit it alone as `test(AUD-NNN): ...`.
3. Run `scripts/evidence.sh AUD-NNN-before`.
4. Fix the code. Commit as `fix(AUD-NNN): ...`.
5. Run `scripts/evidence.sh AUD-NNN-after`.
6. Fill in all four sections of the issue file. Do not set Status to fixed without both evidence runs.

In "Why the AI made the mistake", only state what the transcript or code shows. If you are guessing, start the line with `Hypothesis:`.

## Secrets

- Never read `.env` or print private keys, RPC keys or API keys. AI transcripts in this repo are committed to git.
- Only testnet burner wallets are used in this project.

## Commit message prefixes

| Prefix | Use for |
|---|---|
| `ai:` | Code generated by an AI tool and committed with little or no human change |
| `human:` | Code written or substantially rewritten by a person |
| `test(AUD-NNN):` | Regression test for an issue |
| `fix(AUD-NNN):` | Fix for an issue |
| `docs:` | Spec, report, issue files |
| `evidence:` | Evidence runs, testnet logs |
| `chore:` | Tooling and config |

## Rules learned from audit findings

Append a rule here each time an audit finding shows the AI making a mistake it could repeat. Every rule must cite the issue it came from. This section is part of our specification engineering evidence, so never delete old rules; mark them superseded instead.

- AUD-004: A whitelist mapping alone does not restrict ERC-20 movement. Enforce sender and recipient eligibility in OpenZeppelin's transfer hook and execute a direct-transfer regression; skipped tests are not passing behavioral evidence. Apply the latest explicit requirements when revocation semantics differ from the historical spec.
- AUD-005: Before testing an invariant, check it against every later requirements file. If a later requirement makes it false, restate it in the spec in the same change. Never name a test after an invariant unless the test would fail when that invariant is broken.
- AUD-006: A stored `issuer` or owner field is not proof of authority. Test every role path that touches it (grant, revoke, renounce, hand-over) and any state, such as escrowed tokens, that becomes unrecoverable when the role is gone.
- AUD-007: "No `receive`/`fallback`" does not mean "cannot receive ETH": `selfdestruct` and coinbase rewards force it in. For every contract that holds ETH, test forced ETH, and provide a way to recover any balance above what is owed.
- AUD-008: Implement each function against both the §5 function table and the §3 roles table. A role restriction stated only in §3 is still a revert condition.
- AUD-006, AUD-007: Write a regression's behaviour assertion first and await it (e.g. `await expect(tx).to.revert(ethers)`), then assert the error name. A test that fails only because an error or function is missing from the ABI does not show a behavioural failure, and an un-awaited transaction can leak into the next test.
- AUD-009: Preserve multi-transaction form input across public registry refreshes. Separately invalidate account-dependent data on wallet/chain changes; test approval and deposit as two consecutive user actions.
- AUD-010: A receipt timeout is not a failed transaction. Preserve its hash, keep duplicate submission blocked, and verify an actual receipt before reporting success or a revert.
- AUD-011: An `npm ci` that passes proves the lockfile works only on the machine that wrote it. After any dependency change, keep `test/FrontendLockfile.regression.test.ts` passing (every optional dependency has a lock entry). Do not claim a clean install for other platforms unless one was actually run there.
- AUD-012: A passing test suite does not show that the code has room to grow. Before tagging any change to a contract that `AssetFactory` deploys, record the runtime bytecode size of all three contracts against the EIP-170 limit (24 576 bytes) in the evidence. Deploy to public networks only with the optimised `production` profile.
- AUD-013: Adding an event or a new path that emits an existing event changes what every log consumer shows. When a contract change adds either, find each frontend or script that reads that contract's events, and test that it labels the new operation correctly.

# AUD-012: AssetFactory is exactly at the EIP-170 size limit because the Sepolia deploy uses the unoptimised profile

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | fixed |
| Severity | low |
| Category | other (deployment / contract size) |
| Found by (method) | manual review: bytecode size measurement after the D5 tests passed |
| Found by (person) | Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), session 069871d2, the same session that generated D5 |
| Location | `package.json` `deploy:sepolia` script; `hardhat.config.ts` `default` profile; at 714366d (tag `ai-baseline-d5`) |
| AI session that produced the code | Script and profiles: Phase 1 setup session (`exports/2026-10-23-phase1-setup.txt`, commit 9884a9b). Size growth: D5, session 069871d2 |
| Baseline commit | 714366d |
| Regression test commit | 1e849ec |
| Fix commit | 74af940 |

## What is wrong

`AssetFactory` deploys `AssetToken` and `AssetSale` with `new`, so its runtime bytecode contains both contracts' creation code. `hardhat.config.ts` defines two build profiles. `default` has no optimizer settings; `production` enables the optimizer with 200 runs. `hardhat run` uses `default` unless `--build-profile` is given, and `deploy:sepolia` passes no profile:

```json
"deploy:sepolia": "hardhat run scripts/deploy.ts --network sepolia"
```

| Build | AssetFactory runtime bytes | Share of EIP-170 limit (24 576) |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 3, default profile (`docs/evidence/phase3/bytecode-sizes.txt`) | 22 557 | 91.8% |
| main at bff2f81, default profile | 23 418 | 95.3% |
| D5 at 714366d, default profile | **24 576** | **100.0%, 0 bytes headroom** |
| D5 at 714366d, production profile | 13 545 | 55.1% |

`docs/evidence/aud-012/deploy-before.log` runs `hardhat run scripts/deploy.ts` without a profile, as `deploy:sepolia` does. The factory it compiles is 24 576 bytes. EIP-170 rejects code only when it is *more* than 24 576 bytes, so this build still deploys today. The test suite deploys it too.

## 1. Why the AI made the mistake

What the code and transcripts show:
- The Phase 1 session wrote both profiles and the profile-less `deploy:sepolia` script in commit 9884a9b. Nothing in the repo links the two. The `production` profile was never used by any script.
- The Phase 3 session measured the factory at 22 557 bytes and wrote "It fits, but little headroom remains. The `production` build profile enables the optimiser" (`docs/phase3-implementation.md:93`). It recorded the risk but did not change the deploy script or open an issue.
- The D5 session (this one) added `Pausable` and `forcedTransfer` to `AssetToken`. That grew the factory by 1 158 bytes. The session ran the full test suite before measuring size and only found the problem afterwards. The size was not checked as part of implementing D5, although Phase 3's note was in the files the session had read.

Hypothesis: a passing test run reads as "deployable" because the in-process network enforces EIP-170. That hides how close the code is to the limit, since tests fail only once the limit is actually exceeded.

## 2. Why it is a problem

With no headroom left, the next change to `AssetToken`, `AssetSale` or `AssetFactory` will make `AssetFactory` larger than 24 576 bytes. That includes any fix from the coming D5 review. Its deployment would then revert on Sepolia and locally, which blocks AUD-003 (the outstanding Sepolia deploy) and the demo. The unoptimised build also costs more gas to deploy and call. There is no security impact, and nothing fails at 714366d itself.

## 3. How we fixed it

74af940 changes `deploy:sepolia` to `hardhat run --build-profile production scripts/deploy.ts --network sepolia` and updates the usage comment in `scripts/deploy.ts`. Local scripts and tests keep the `default` profile, so the gas and coverage figures in earlier evidence runs stay comparable.

Not changed (user decision, 4 November 2026): the `default` profile stays unoptimised. Local deploys (`deploy:local`, `deploy:ephemeral`) still use the 24 576-byte build. The regression test guards the Sepolia path only.

New CLAUDE.md rule: see the AUD-012 entry under "Rules learned from audit findings".

## 4. Evidence the fix works

- Regression test: `test/DeployProfile.regression.test.ts` :: `deploy:sepolia builds with a profile that enables the optimizer for every compiler`. It reads the profile from the actual `deploy:sepolia` script and checks Hardhat's resolved config for that profile.
- Before: `docs/evidence/runs/20261104T055346Z_1e849ec-dirty_AUD-012-before/test.log` (128 passing, 1 failing: `"default" solc 0.8.24 optimizer: expected undefined to equal true`); `docs/evidence/aud-012/deploy-before.log` (24 576-byte factory).
- After: `docs/evidence/runs/20261104T055527Z_74af940-dirty_AUD-012-after/test.log` (129 passing; coverage 98.79% lines); `docs/evidence/aud-012/deploy-after.log`: the same deploy script with `--build-profile production` deploys a 13 545-byte factory.
- Not verified: an actual Sepolia deployment (still outstanding under AUD-003).

# D5 implementation and review: pause and forced transfer

Date: 3–4 November 2026. Tool: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), session 069871d2, directed by Chordia Laksh. The transcript is archived by the hook under `docs/ai-logs/raw/`.

## What was decided

D5 was opened on 23 October 2026 and decided on 3 November 2026. Pause and forced transfer are implemented. Freeze is dropped, because whitelist revocation already blocks a holder from sending, receiving and buying. The normative rows are spec-v1 §5 "D5 functions", with invariants 1, 5, 6 and 7 restated. The reasons are in `docs/spec/phase3-requirements.md`, "D5 decision". Claude Code proposed each option, and the user adopted every recommendation.

## What was built (tag `ai-baseline-d5`, 714366d)

| Spec row / invariant | Implementation |
|---|---|
| `pause()` / `unpause()`, caller `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` | OpenZeppelin `Pausable`. `_update` calls `_requireNotPaused()`, so `transfer`, `transferFrom` and AssetSale's `allocate`, `buyTokens` and `recoverUnsoldTokens` revert with `EnforcedPause` |
| `forcedTransfer(from, to, amount)`, caller `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` | Reverts with `ForcedTransferFromZeroAddress` (a zero source would mint), `ForcedTransferFromWhitelisted(from)` or `RecipientNotWhitelisted(to)`. Calls ERC20's `_update` directly, which bypasses pause and the sender check. Emits `Transfer` and `ForcedTransfer` |
| Invariants 5, 6, 7 | `test/AssetToken.D5.test.ts` (21 tests after review), including a pairwise sweep of every source and recipient for invariant 6 |

Mutation check (`docs/evidence/d5/mutation.log`): removing the pause check, the zero-source check or the whitelisted-source check, or routing `forcedTransfer` through the overridden `_update`, makes the D5 suite fail. All 4 of 4 mutants were killed.

## Review before merge

This review was done by the same session that wrote the code, so it is **not independent**. Audit-1 had the same limitation. It covered the contract diff against spec-v1 §3 and §5, the CLAUDE.md rules, and every frontend consumer of the token's ABI and events.

| Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|
| AssetFactory runtime is exactly 24 576 bytes (EIP-170 limit) on the unoptimised profile used by `deploy:sepolia` | [AUD-012](issues/AUD-012-assetfactory-is-exactly-at-the-eip-170-size-limit-.md), fixed: the Sepolia deploy uses the `production` profile (13 545 bytes) |
| History shows a forced transfer as an ordinary `Transfer` sent by the holder | [AUD-013](issues/AUD-013-transaction-history-shows-a-forced-transfer-as-an-.md), fixed |
| D5 tests covered granting `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` but not revoking or renouncing it (CLAUDE.md AUD-006 rule) | Tests added in f1c1534. They pass, so there is no defect |
| Contract logic against the D5 table: caller, preconditions, events and every revert condition | No defect found |

Observations, not changed in this merge:
- **Delegating `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` now delegates confiscation.** A delegated admin can grant itself `COMPLIANCE_ROLE`, revoke a holder and force-transfer their balance to any whitelisted address. Before D5, the most it could do was block a holder. The frontend never grants this role (it only restores `COMPLIANCE_ROLE` to the connected wallet), but a direct contract call can. The trust model in spec-v1 §1 ("the issuer is trusted") now extends to anyone the issuer makes an admin.
- **Paused-token errors are generic.** The frontend shows "Contract rejected the request: EnforcedPause." because `frontend/src/utils/errors.ts` has no message for it. The UI has no pause or forced-transfer controls, and spec-v1 §7 does not require any.
- **The default profile has 0 bytes of headroom.** AUD-012 fixed the Sepolia path only. Any further growth in `AssetToken`, `AssetSale` or `AssetFactory` makes local deploys and the test suite fail until the optimizer is enabled for `default`.
- **`evidence.sh` leaves coverage-instrumented artifacts** (factory 31 817 bytes). `npm run test:integration` deploys straight from `artifacts/`, so after an evidence run it fails at factory deployment until `npx hardhat compile --force` is run. This predates D5.

## Results at merge

- Contracts: 131 passing, line coverage 98.79%. Evidence run: `docs/evidence/runs/20261104T060834Z_f1c1534-dirty_AUD-013-after/`. "-dirty" refers to uncommitted session transcripts and docs only.
- Frontend: 113 tests passed (`docs/evidence/aud-013/frontend-tests-after.log`). The build succeeds.
- Local integration lifecycle against a real Hardhat node: passes, including the new forced-transfer and pause steps (`docs/evidence/aud-013/integration-after.log`).
- Not done: a real Sepolia deployment (AUD-003), and browser or MetaMask checks of the new behaviour.

- The integration test passes against a real local node.
- Coverage still works with the optimizer on.
